name: What is the difference between structural remodeling and cosmetic remodeling?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between structural remodeling and cosmetic remodeling in a home renovation?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between structural remodeling and cosmetic remodeling in a home renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Structural remodeling affects how the home stands up, not just how it looks. Common examples include removing load-bearing walls, enlarging openings, reinforcing floors, relocating stairs, or adding beams and headers. Cosmetic remodeling keeps the existing structure intact and focuses on finishes and surfaces, such as repainting, replacing flooring, updating cabinets, or installing new countertops. The distinction matters because structural work usually requires engineering, permits, inspections, and higher budgets, while cosmetic work is often faster and simpler to approve. Many homeowners in Los Angeles and nearby cities search this distinction when planning open-concept layouts or home additions because the difference determines whether plans need a structural engineer and city review. If a project changes framing or load paths in any way, it should be treated as structural rather than cosmetic.
acceptedAnswer.description: Structural remodeling changes the building’s frame, support system, or load path, such as removing walls, adding beams, or altering openings. Cosmetic remodeling changes the appearance only, such as paint, flooring, cabinets, fixtures, or tile, without affecting the structure.
